newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy senate approves communications law.
newsitem.headline: Italy senate approves communications law.

text.p: Italy's Senate (upper house) on Thursday gave its approval to a law which includes the creation of a watchdog authority for the communications sector.
The law will now have to go to the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) for final approval. The watchdog body is a prerequisite for the privatisation of state telecommunications holding Stet.
Stet is due to be merged with its operating unit Telecom Italia and sold off later this year.
Legislators gave an initial approval to the first article of the law, the part which sets up the watchdog, on Wednesday night during individual votes on parts of the bill.
On Thursday they approved the entire package, enabling it to move on the lower house.
The other parts of the law include sections on anti-trust in the television sector, the assignment of television frequencies and the regulation of pay television. -- Rome newsroom +396-678-2501
